study.question: Does exposing activity action-pair context when target matching support is absent or singular help prediction, and does pair identity contribute beyond the same added scalar mass?
study.hypothesis: The final relative-gap symmetric activity readout is unnecessarily suppressed by a target-match common-support gate. For positive known target fields with at least two activity timestamp groups but at most one target-matching group, opening that readout preserves useful coarse activity pair context. A structured extension should beat both the unchanged incumbent and an extension with identical total off-diagonal mass distributed uniformly over12 pair coordinates. This is a local hypothesis; activity context may also be irrelevant or harmful without target repetition.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit local field-adapted attention; this proposal changes only availability of deterministic activity statistics at the classifier. Original DIN abandons softmax normalization; local backbone retains it. No DIN reproduction or global novelty claim.
Only field-availability warning verified. No item matching objective adopted; no item journey or full-paper comparison claimed.

Earlier same-study fallback opened pooled-action rank only where same-action rank lacked support. Current extension exposes an existing24-column symmetric activity pair/relative-gap readout for fields lacking repeated target matches, with an equal-mass identity-removal control.

study.proposed_difference: Let C=1[target_groups>1 and activity_groups>1], E=1[activity_groups>1], A=E-C. Both preserve final24 incumbent inputs on C. Candidate adds .5*A*h*S_offdiag; control adds exactly the same per-field offdiagonal total divided equally over12 coordinates. Positive target and valid field/type requirements remain inherited; missing targets are never enabled. Earlier24 unweighted pair coordinates retain C. New modes compute both tables with no added trainable parameter/RNG/optimizer/loss change. This tests support extension plus action-pair identity, not a new event stream or item path.
predictions: Candidate-supplied first512 diagnostics will show nonzero E-C and zero subset/common-prefix errors; support fraction remains descriptive.
Structured extension should exceed unchanged incumbent in full-population validation AUC; compare Logloss and host-measured cost as secondary outcomes.
Structured extension should exceed equal-mass extension if individual pair identity has incremental utility; equality would leave a generic branch-activation/intensity explanation.

Exploratory host category-match-absent/short-history slices may show larger differences, but these are imperfect proxies for E-C and not predeclared causal subgroup tests. No significance claim without paired repetition.
falsifiers: No additional valid E-C fields or materially zero added mass makes the intervention inactive.
Structured extension fails to improve incumbent AUC under frozen matched protocol: no support for predictive benefit in this implementation, even if control is worse.
Equal-mass control matches or exceeds structured extension: pair-identity explanation unsupported, even if both improve incumbent.

Nonzero common-support preservation, parent-prefix, missing-target, unsupported or total-mass identity errors invalidate attribution and require a corrected implementation with all failed costs retained.
Gains vanish/reverse in paired repetitions or require greater measured cost: withhold robust mechanism/efficiency claims.
alternative_explanations: Additional activity features may be noise when no target repetition exists; suppression may be beneficial regularization.
Scalar offdiagonal switching mass, changed activation prevalence or gradient conditioning may explain improvement; equal-mass control addresses identity but not all optimization effects.
Rare actions, missing fields, common target support and history truncation select different populations; E-C is not random or causal.
Shared classifier training can alter predictions on old common support even when inputs there are identical; report host overall/slices, do not claim model-level invariance.
Uniform control preserves mass and parameter capacity but intentionally removes within-field variation and changes feature geometry.
Single adaptive seed, repeated validation selection and checkpoint selection noise may explain differences.
No target information is required beyond inherited positive-ID validity; target-specific relevance could remain essential.
